title: Ephemeral backpressure feedback loop — hosted API postmortem (P0)
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-04-07 at ~09:13 UTC we observed a rapid, system-wide amplification of tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors for the Hosted API streaming and unary endpoints. The incident lasted ~47 minutes with partial degradation continuing in a small cohort of customers until 2029-04-07 10:05 UTC. Impact: P0 — many customers experienced slow streaming chunks (high TTFB and stall/reconnects) and an increase in 500/503 responses for short generator requests. Root cause: a feedback loop between the edge multiplexing layer's backpressure signal and the serving pool's adaptive batching/coalescer. Under a surge of short, high-concurrency requests, the edge applied a flow-control backoff which increased per-connection buffering. The serving pool's adaptive coalescer interpreted longer queue latencies as signal to widen batching windows, increasing scheduling latency and causing queue pileup; that in turn intensified the backpressure signal, amplifying latency and leading to request timeouts and 5xx. Secondary contributor: an interaction with a recent KV-cache eviction optimization (PR #3987) that increased cold-KV misses for concurrent prefixes, adding CPU spikes to serving nodes.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 09:12 — Synthetic and customer SLO alarms triggered: p95 TTFB crossing alert threshold for hosted-api-streaming.
- 09:13 — Alerts escalated to on-call. First signs: elevated acceptor queue lengths at the edge (dashboards).
- 09:15 — 5xx rate climbed from baseline 0.02% to 1.8% across regions. Streaming clients logged increased chunk latency and reconnects.
- 09:18 — On-call disabled new rollout of adaptive-coalescer v2 via feature flag (rollback started).
- 09:20 — Rollback completed for coalescer; partial improvement in p95 but tail (p99/p999) stayed high.
- 09:27 — Discovered elevated KV-cache miss rate and CPU spikes on a subset of serving hosts correlated with the hotspots.
- 09:30 — Temporary mitigations: edge backpressure aggressiveness reduced (increase ack window), and a serving-side short-circuit was applied to limit coalescing delay to 6ms.
- 09:40 — Observed sustained decline in 5xx and tail-latency; reconnects reduced.
- 10:05 — Incident declared mitigated; monitoring continued for residual regressions.

Impact:
- Duration (major impact): ~09:13–09:40 UTC (27 minutes), residual until 10:05 UTC.
- Customer-visible: increased latency and transient 5xx for streaming and short unary workloads. Estimated affected requests: ~180k requests with ~2.1% receiving 5xx during peak.
- Internal system: acceptor queue depth at edge peaked at 6x baseline; p99 TTFB increased by ~8x in affected regions.

Root cause analysis (detailed):
1) Adaptive coalescer policy regression: a change in adaptive coalescer v2 increased the dynamic batching window upper bound from 12ms -> 40ms in low-throughput, high-concurrency conditions (intended to improve throughput). Under this workload pattern (many short-lived streams and small token counts), the wider window allowed coalescing to delay scheduling meaningfully, increasing per-request latency.
2) Edge backpressure miscalibration: the edge multiplexer signals a congestion backoff when acceptor queue depth and per-connection buffer exceed thresholds. The aggressive setting for backpressure (recently tuned to reduce dropped connections during other incidents) reduced upstream transmission and made connection buffers grow at the edge. Larger buffers cause upstream perceived latencies, feeding the coalescer's heuristic to widen further.
3) KV-cache eviction optimization (PR #3987): this optimization aggressively evicted less-frequent prefixes to reduce memory; combined with a short surge of similar prefixes, miss storms caused extra CPU and I/O on serving nodes, making them respond slower and exacerbating queueing.
4) Lack of an explicit upper limit on coalescer-induced scheduling delay: there was no hard cap to prevent coalescing windows from growing beyond a safe threshold for latency-sensitive workloads.

Contributing process/system gaps:
- Feature flagging incomplete: coalescer v2 rollout was targeted but telemetry gating (small-sample AB test) did not catch this workload pattern because synthetic traffic did not reproduce the short-high-concurrency mix.
- Runbook gap: no immediate playbook existed for a backpressure-coalescer interaction scenario — operators relied on ad-hoc heuristics.
- Observability: KV-cache miss storm correlated graphs were present but buried under default dashboard noise; no high-visibility alert for sudden miss-rate multipliers.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Feature-flag rollback of adaptive coalescer v2 across serving pools (owner: Kai Morgan). Rolled back by 09:20 UTC.
- Edge-backpressure tune: increased ack window and throttled backpressure aggressiveness to reduce buffer growth (owner: Miguel Torres).
- Short-term coalescer cap: deployed a hotfix limiting coalescing delay to <=6ms for streaming/unary short path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4112) (owner: Evelyn Zhang).
- KV-cache eviction reverted for affected fleet slice and eviction parameters relaxed (owner: Jordan Lee).

Permanent fixes and actions (timeline and owners):
- Short-term (1 week):
  - Add a hard upper-bound configuration (configurable) to coalescer delay for latency-sensitive routes (owner: Evelyn) — ETA 2029-04-13.
  - Add a realtime KV-cache miss-rate multiplier alert with a runbook to auto-scale cache or temporarily relax eviction (owner: Jordan) — ETA 2029-04-14.
  - Improve feature flag rollout gating: add synthetic scenario for short-high-concurrency streaming patterns to preflight tests (owner: Kai) — ETA 2029-04-12.
- Medium-term (1–2 months):
  - Implement a closed-loop guard in the edge that prevents backpressure from pushing buffers beyond x% of per-connection memory or time (owner: Miguel) — ETA 2029-05-22.
  - Rework adaptive coalescer heuristics to incorporate edge buffer and KV-cache health signals as inputs to avoid contradictory actions (owner: Serving Runtime team) — ETA 2029-05-30.
  - Post-incident capacity test: synthetic spike tests that combine KV-cache cold patterns with short-stream surges to validate heuristics and runbooks (owner: SRE QA) — ETA 2029-05-10.
- Long-term:
  - Replace ad-hoc coalescer policy toggles with tiered scheduling profiles (latency-sensitive vs throughput-optimized) and automatic profile routing based on customer routing tags (owner: Product + Serving Runtime) — ETA Q3 2029.
  - Run a cross-team incident learning workshop to refine guardrails and observability across edge/serving/cache boundaries (owner: Eng SRE leads) — ETA Q3 2029.

Runbook draft (actions for next P0 detection of similar patterns):
1) Triage: check acceptor queue depths at edge, p99 TTFB, and streaming chunk latency.
2) Immediately toggle adaptive coalescer -> safe-mode via feature flag for affected pools.
3) If 5xx rate > 0.5% and p99 TTFB > 3x baseline: reduce edge backpressure aggressiveness (increase ack window) and enable coalescer cap.
4) If KV-cache miss multiplier > 4x baseline: revert eviction tuning for the slice and scale cache nodes.
5) Notify product and hosting teams; open a postmortem ticket and tag owners from Serving Runtime and Edge teams.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did synthetic preflight not cover the short-high-concurrency streaming pattern? (Action: Kai to expand preflight scenarios).
- Do we need an automated circuit-breaker that disables adaptive batching heuristics when the edge signals buffer growth? (Action: Evelyn + Miguel to prototype).
- Investigate whether the KV-cache eviction policy change was properly annotated in the rollout notes and telemetry (Action: Jordan).

Monitoring/dashboard checklist to add/change:
- Add a combined dashboard widget: edge acceptor queue depth + coalescer window size + kv-cache miss multiplier for correlated visualization.
- New alert: KV-cache miss multiplier > 4x sustained 60s.
- New alert: coalescer effective delay > 12ms for latency routes.

Post-incident notes and comms:
- Incident review scheduled: 2029-04-11 16:00 UTC (SRE + Serving Runtime + Edge + Product).
- Customer communication: status update sent to affected customers during incident and follow-up summary to those customers by 2029-04-09.

Appendix (quick-reference telemetry snippets):
- Peak p99 TTFB: 1.8s (baseline 220ms)
- 5xx rate at peak: 1.8% (baseline 0.02%)
- Estimated affected requests: ~180k
- Hot hosts: serving-pool-7a, serving-pool-7c showed >6x CPU and miss multipliers.

Owners and contacts:
- Incident owner / SRE on-call: Aisha Patel
- Edge oncall: Miguel Torres
- Serving Runtime lead: Evelyn Zhang
- Cache lead: Jordan Lee
- Follow-up coordinator: Kai Morgan

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working draft; please add any missing signal links, reproduce steps, and assign owners for medium/long-term actions. We should capture the exact feature-flag toggles and full rollback diffs into the JIRA ticket SRE-2029 for traceability.
